sectors.trend: Banks led ASX 200 recovery but face deteriorating credit quality: 15% drop in home loan applications, 18-yr high mortgage stress, record house price fall forecasts. Net interest margin tailwind from rate hikes offset by credit loss provisions.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher rates short-term but face rising NPLs and provision costs within 6-12 months. Housing downturn is the key swing factor.

sectors.trend: Active exploration pipeline: Macarthur WA iron ore bulk test cleared, Lindian 20-yr Kazakhstan rare earths offtake, Dalaroo 12,000m African gold drill, True North Qld copper expansion, PLC WA Murchison gold. Iron ore and rare earths themes supportive.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX benefit from iron ore demand; small-caps (LND.AX, DLR.AX, TNR.AX, PLC.AX) offer speculative upside. Rare earths offtake supports supply-chain security narrative.

sectors.trend: TMK Energy gas rates surge on Mongolian drilling; Persian Gulf tanker fires spike oil risk premium; energy transition costs 'running off rails'; One Nation coal plant pressure creates policy uncertainty.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, SXG.AX, ALE.AX face volatile gas pricing. Oil-linked names (WES.AX, BHP.AX oil division) benefit from Gulf risk premium. Coal policy risk weighs on energy transition equities.

sectors.trend: Hundreds of regional doctors strike over poor conditions; Ozempic maker (Novo Nordisk) in trouble with tablet alternatives emerging; childcare chain closures continue.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, WES.AX (pharmacy) face mixed signals. Regional doctor strike pressures public health system, potentially boosting private providers. Ozempic disruption may shift GLP-1 market dynamics.

sectors.trend: Housing affordability crisis deepens; Melbourne councils admit inability to cope with population growth; retail theft ('shooshies') rising; Qantas A380 NFL 49ers tour signals consumer event spending.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) pressured by housing downturn and rental market stress. Consumer staples (WES.AX, WDW.AX) see defensive rotation. Property developers face overhang.

sectors.trend: Nvidia $13B Hugging Face acquisition confirms AI capex cycle; data centre backlash intensifies; AI integration across payments (Mastercard, Flywire) and industrials (Danaher).
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX exposure but supports sentiment for CSL.AX (AI in diagnostics), SSG.AX, and infrastructure names. Data centre NIMBY risk could delay Australian cloud buildout.

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and property developer exposure; favour banks with strong capital buffers (CBA.AX, NAB.AX); monitor NPL trends quarterly
Hedge rate sensitivity with long-duration bonds; favour dividend-paying defensives; monitor CPI and employment data closely
Maintain energy sector allocation (WES.AX, BHP.AX); monitor Brent crude; consider oil-linked hedges
Favour companies with pricing power and automation exposure; avoid margin-compressed sectors
Diversify across fossil and renewable energy; monitor One Nation political influence on coal policy
Monitor CSL.AX, SGH.AX for any supply-chain or demand impact from regional doctor strike

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely range-bound to modestly lower over 1-3 months. Banking sector provides floor support but housing stress and rate hike fears cap upside. Geopolitical oil risk adds volatility. Expect 2-4% downside risk if RBA hikes again.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautious. Productivity 'bad to worse' and housing correction weigh on growth. Mining pipeline and rare earths theme offer structural upside. Energy transition cost overruns create policy whiplash. Net: flat to modestly positive for quality large-caps, negative for rate-sensitive and property-linked names.
